topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and confer clonal advantages that can lead to cancer in a permissive cellular environment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being simply a matter of bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: How environmental mutagens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of becoming mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate.

topics.label: Carcinogen specificity and a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of carcinogenic mechanisms by explaining susceptibility in particular tissue and developmental contexts before summarising that account.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and why establishing carcinogenicity remains difficult.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions and frames their practical implications as decisions about risks and benefits.
